chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Vaudeville versus cabaret and the theatre circuits
summary: He distinguishes after-hours cabaret from daytime and nighttime vaudeville, and says only theatres ran in chain circuits like Orpheum and Loew's.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: when you first started out you were performing in vaudeville, not in cabaret.
And how did you distinguish between vaudeville and cabaret? What's the difference?

Well, the cabaret is after hours, it's in the night time after hours and vaudeville is a daytime and nighttime situation. You do different shows in the daytime and different shows at night. But the vaudeville has a bill of variety acts, one after another. Night clubs don't have that. Now, you've been to them. I know you have. It's like going to see a TV show and like going to see a vaudeville show. Now a vaudeville show is different than a TV show but they use the same talent.
Well, the circuits that you were going on, were they in vaudeville or cabaret circuits? You mentioned a number of different circuits.

No that's a cabaret in a cabaret --no circuit. They didn't have a circuit lined up that way. There's just cabaret dates in town, but no circuit. Like the theater, you've got theaters all over town but there's a circuit. 'Cause the owners have a chain of theaters. Orpheum has a chain, Pantages has a chain, Poli had a chain, Loews had a chain.
And the entertainment that was done on the chains was primarily variety shows, basically.
